title: A freely scalable adversary is different from fixed reaction rates
statement: For fixed finite baseline rates and allowed excess support, uniform positive TERMINAL target probability at every fixed t>0 over ALL initial types and ALL freely selectable nonanticipative nonexplosive finite-rate excess controls holds iff the rank criterion succeeds. Failed pruning gives finite-rate reset policy; target departure gives p(t)<=exp(-Kt)p(0)+(Qmax/K)(1-exp(-Kt)). Infimum over K tending infinity is a sequence of finite chains, not an infinite-rate process. Success at maximal acquired rank L has uniform small-time power Theta(t^L); sharp reset-parent suppression pays skip probability O((1+t)/K), and arrival needs L baseline rings. Optional no-deletion population scale (Ktarget/n)^(1/L) holds only stated small-time/uniform-control regime and is not an expectation claim. No necessity for one fixed physical network or optimal chemical reset exponent follows.

requires: Genuine non-double-counted allocated progress subgenerators, collateral safety, bounded adverse batch size and actual per-label predictable participation; regularity/nonexplosion for Dynkin localization.

Each theorem retains its own fixed-population or admissible immigration/pure-deletion seed contract, actual first-terminal stopping and output loss, frozen ordinary labels, exact trace clock and reward-weighted potential.

Uniform/null-slot reset and without-replacement sampling laws for exact carried profiles; a matching mean alone is insufficient. Abstract control converses require free nonnegative finite-rate intensities with no common upper bound.
